aliases: CBRE Global Infrastructure Fund Holdings I, LP
CBRE Caledon Global Infrastructure Fund Holdings I, LP
funds.directEquityBasis: CBRE Investment Management describes the strategy as direct private infrastructure investing, and public-utility ownership filings identify the fund's master vehicle as an indirect equity owner of WANRack, LLC and of the upstream infrastructure vehicle that owns GW Operating, LLC.

northAmericaQualification.rationale: Pennsylvania and Georgia utility filings attribute current ownership of the U.S. fiber-network operator WANRack, LLC and its affiliate GW Operating, LLC to CBRE Global Infrastructure Fund Holdings I, LP; the Georgia filing states that the internal restructuring does not change ultimate ownership or control.

snapshot.investmentStrategy: Evergreen global direct private infrastructure strategy targeting mid-market core and core-plus OECD assets across digital infrastructure, energy transition and transportation.

evidence.title: Global Direct Private Infrastructure
evidence.evidenceLabel: Current global direct private infrastructure strategy
evidence.evidenceSummary: The current strategy page describes direct investments through pooled vehicles and separately managed accounts in mid-market core and core-plus infrastructure across the Americas, EMEA and Asia-Pacific, including renewable energy, transportation, digital, social and utility assets.

evidence.title: CBRE IM awarded £500 million global real estate mandate by Wales Pension Partnership
evidence.evidenceSummary: CBRE Investment Management states that Wales Pension Partnership had invested in the CBRE Global Infrastructure Fund in the prior year, confirming the commercial fund name and continuing institutional use.

evidence.title: Sabius Private Equity Fund — Q2 2025 Report
evidence.evidenceSummary: The institutional report identifies CBRE Global Infrastructure Fund as a diversified global open-end fund investing in mid-market core and core-plus infrastructure in OECD countries, with digital infrastructure, energy transition and transportation themes.

evidence.title: Form ADV — CBRE Investment Management Infrastructure Inc.
evidence.publisher: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission Investment Adviser Public Disclosure
evidence.evidenceSummary: The annual amendment lists CBRE Global Infrastructure Fund Holdings I, LP as the master private infrastructure fund, reports $5,102,216,829 of current gross asset value for the arrangement, and lists related feeder and aggregator entities. The filing date is used as the reporting date because no separate valuation date is stated.

evidence.title: WANRack, LLC and WANRack Holdings, LLC — Pennsylvania Public Utility Commission filing
evidence.evidenceSummary: The filing describes WANRack as a private fiber wide-area-network operator across 23 U.S. states and identifies CBRE Global Infrastructure Fund Holdings I, LP as an 88% indirect owner; it also records the former CBRE Caledon master-fund and adviser names.

evidence.title: WANRack, LLC and GW Operating, LLC — Georgia Public Service Commission pro forma transfer filing
evidence.evidenceLabel: Current ownership and unchanged ultimate control
evidence.evidenceSummary: The filing states that WANRack operates in 23 states, charts CBRE Global Infrastructure Fund Holdings I, LP as holding 97.6% of the upstream infrastructure vehicle, and states that the internal restructuring will not change ultimate ownership or control of WANRack and GW Operating.

funds.repoDispositionRationale: FUND-054 matches the same evergreen commercial vehicle, but the repository uses an abbreviated fund name, an unsupported undated $3.3B amount, a narrower strategy and sector description, Global-only geography, and an older generic strategy URL; the corrected row preserves the legacy ID and uses the current commercial name, Form ADV gross asset value and reporting date, and fund-attributed U.S. ownership evidence.

excludedCandidates.fundName: CBRE Bright Star Infra Co-Invest LP
excludedCandidates.rationale: Current regulatory filings establish a private infrastructure co-invest vehicle and reported assets, but opened public evidence does not identify its underlying investment, establish a North American mandate or current North American holding, or show that it is commercially distinct from any related vehicle.

The current Form ADV establishes a private infrastructure co-invest vehicle and reported assets, but no opened fund-specific source establishes its underlying investment, North American qualification, lifecycle beyond the filing, or distinct commercial strategy.

SEC and Montana Board of Investments materials establish the legal vehicle and an institutional commitment, but they do not establish whether the mandate is direct rather than indirect, identify a current holding, or prove North American qualification.
The SEC filing establishes the vehicle and offering, but opened evidence does not establish a direct-equity strategy, current North American mandate or holding, or present lifecycle.

excludedCandidates.fundName: CBRE Andromeda Infrastructure Investments IV, LP
excludedCandidates.rationale: The SEC filing establishes the vehicle and offering, but no opened fund-specific primary source establishes direct-equity infrastructure scope, North American qualification, current holdings, or current lifecycle.

unresolvedConflicts.subject: CBRE Bright Star Infra Co-Invest LP and CBRE Starlight Infra Co-Invest LP
unresolvedConflicts.issue: The current Form ADV confirms both vehicles and their reported gross asset values, but public evidence does not identify their underlying assets, establish North American exposure, or resolve whether they are separate commercial co-invest strategies or related parallel vehicles.
unresolvedConflicts.recommendedResolution: Obtain current audited financial statements, LP reports or a manager vehicle chart identifying each underlying investment, mandate, lifecycle and relationship between the two vehicles.

unresolvedConflicts.subject: CBRE customized infrastructure mandate vehicles
unresolvedConflicts.issue: Musselshell, Minke and Andromeda IV are documented legal vehicles, but the opened filings and LP materials do not establish direct-versus-indirect strategy, current asset attribution, North American qualification, or whether each is independently managed rather than a sleeve or customized account.
unresolvedConflicts.recommendedResolution: Obtain fund-specific offering memoranda, LP investment memoranda, audited reports or manager confirmation covering strategy, geography, current holdings and commercial vehicle identity.

unresolvedConflicts.subject: CBRE Global Infrastructure Fund gross asset value date
unresolvedConflicts.issue: The 2026 Form ADV reports $5,102,216,829 of current gross asset value in the annual amendment filed on 2026-03-31, but the public filing does not separately state the underlying valuation date; the snapshot therefore uses the filing date as the amount's reporting date rather than inferring a valuation date.
unresolvedConflicts.recommendedResolution: Confirm the valuation date and period-end gross asset value from the fund's audited financial statements or a manager-issued investor report.

notes: The master fund and eight Form ADV feeder or aggregator entities are treated as one commercial fund rather than separate vehicles.
North American qualification rests on fund-specific regulatory ownership of WANRack and GW Operating, not on the generic Global or OECD label.
The SEC amount is current gross asset value reported in the 2026 annual Form ADV, not commitments or a final close.
Customized and co-invest vehicles without fund-specific directness, lifecycle and North American evidence remain excluded pending further documentation.
Global Indirect Private Infrastructure and listed infrastructure securities products were reviewed and excluded as non-direct strategies.

The IAPD Form ADV did not render in the web viewer because of its file content type but was downloaded and reviewed; Pennsylvania and Georgia filings supplied the opened fund-attributed ownership evidence.
